title: Slow-cooker mashed potatoes
subtitle: Creamy mash made hands-free in the slow cooker
excerpt: Potatoes cooked until very tender in the slow cooker, then mashed with butter and warm milk. Frees up the hob when cooking a large meal.
sourceNotes: Slow-cooker mashed potatoes became popular as a way to free hob space during large roast dinners. The method requires no water; the potatoes steam in a small amount of liquid under the lid.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keep warm in the slow cooker on LOW for up to 1 hour after mashing. Stir in a little extra warm milk before serving.

content.text: The slow cooker steams potatoes rather than boiling them, which means the finished mash is not waterlogged. The potatoes absorb no extra water during cooking. They go in dry and come out very tender and ready to mash. The result is a denser, more flavourful mash than the boiled version.
The method is useful when the hob is occupied with other things. Put the potatoes in the slow cooker and forget about them for 3 to 4 hours. Mash and season before serving.
Use floury potatoes such as Maris Piper or King Edward for the best result. Waxy potatoes will not mash as smoothly.

items.prepNote: peeled and cut into even chunks

content.text: Place {{potato}} of peeled, chunked potatoes in the slow cooker. Add {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt. Pour in 4 tablespoons of water. Place {{unsalted-butter}} of butter on top of the potatoes. Put the lid on and set to HIGH.
Cook for 3 to 4 hours on HIGH, or until a fork passes through the potatoes easily with no resistance.

Drain any liquid from the pot. Mash the potatoes in the slow cooker pot or transfer to a large bowl. Pour in {{whole-milk}} of warm milk and mash until smooth. Season with {{black-pepper-ground}} of black pepper. Taste and adjust the salt. Serve straight away.

rows.symptom: The potatoes are still firm after 4 hours
rows.cause: The chunks were cut too large, or the slow cooker did not reach high enough temperature on HIGH.
rows.fix: Cook for a further hour. Next time cut the potatoes into pieces no larger than 3 cm.

rows.symptom: The mash is gluey and sticky
rows.cause: Waxy potatoes were used, or the potatoes were overworked with an electric mixer.
rows.fix: Use only a manual potato masher. Use floury varieties such as Maris Piper next time.

rows.cause: Not enough milk was added during mashing.
rows.fix: Warm a little more milk and stir it in gradually until you reach the consistency you want.

rows.symptom: The mash has gone cold by serving time
rows.cause: Mash loses heat quickly once out of the pot.
rows.fix: Set the slow cooker to WARM after mashing and keep it there until ready to serve. Stir in a splash of warm milk before serving.

content.text: Mashed potato is a staple side dish in British cooking. It goes with almost everything that produces a gravy or sauce. The slow cooker version does not improve on hob-cooked mash; it makes the same mash while keeping the hob free. It is most useful at Christmas or for Sunday roasts when every burner is occupied.
